# 1 Enoch Chapter 71 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 71:14 — THE MOST DEBATED VERSE IN ALL OF 1 ENOCH

### The Question
Is Enoch being identified AS the Son of Man, or is the Son of Man being presented TO Enoch as a third figure?

### The Two Readings

**Reading A — IDENTIFICATION (LOGOS, PNEUMA):**
> "You are that Son of Man who was born unto righteousness."

The Head of Days (or his representative) speaks directly to Enoch in second person ('you'), identifying Enoch himself as the Son of Man. The entire chapter is then a revelation of Enoch's own identity.

**Reading B — PRESENTATION (EMET):**
> "This is the Son of Man who is born unto righteousness."

The speaker presents a pre-existing, third-figure Son of Man to Enoch. Enoch observes the Son of Man but is not identified with him.

### Manuscript Evidence

| MS Tradition | Reading | Ge'ez Text |
|---|---|---|
| Majority of Ethiopic MSS | "You are" (2nd person) | anta = you |
| Minority MSS / some editions | "This is" (3rd person) | we'etu = he/this |

The majority Ge'ez MSS use the second person 'anta' (you), supporting the identification reading. A minority use 'we'etu' (he/this), supporting the presentation reading.

### Scholarly Positions

| Scholar | Position | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| Nickelsburg & VanderKam | Identification | MS support; contextual second-person sequence in vv. 14-16 |
| Charles (1912) | Presentation | The Son of Man throughout ch. 37-69 is pre-existent; cannot be Enoch |
| Black | Late interpolation | Ch. 70-71 is a later addition that contradicts the earlier Parables |
| Mearns | Contradicts earlier Parables | The pre-existent Son of Man of ch. 46-48 cannot be Enoch |

### Resolution

| Translator | Reading | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "This-is-the-Son-of-Man who-is-born-unto-righteousness" | Minority MS tradition; avoids the identification paradox |
| LOGOS | "You are that Son of Man who was born unto righteousness" | Majority MS tradition; 2nd person throughout vv. 14-16 demands direct address |
| PNEUMA | "You are that Son of Man who was born to righteousness" | Agrees with LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopts the majority reading: **"You are that Son of Man who was born unto righteousness"** (LOGOS/PNEUMA), for the following reasons:

1. **MS support**: The majority of Ge'ez MSS read 'anta' (you), not 'we'etu' (this/he).

2. **Internal grammar**: The entire sequence of vv. 14-16 is in second person ('over you,' 'forsakes you not,' 'proclaims to you,' 'unto you') — if the first clause were 'this is the Son of Man' (referring to a third figure), the sudden shift to second-person address would be grammatically incoherent.

3. **Narrative resolution**: The entire Parables have posed the question of the Son of Man's identity. Ch. 70:1 already said Enoch's name was raised 'to that Son of Man' — the identification is being completed, not introduced.

4. **Theological significance**: The identification of the righteous human being Enoch with the pre-existent heavenly Son of Man is the precise claim that makes this text significant for understanding NT Christology. The text presents this identification as the climax of the entire work.

**EMET's alternative reading** is preserved as a valid minority MS tradition. Readers who follow the 'presentation' reading (e.g., Charles) have textual grounds for their position.

**Status:** RESOLVED in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA based on majority MS support and internal grammatical coherence. EMET's minority reading noted. This is the single most significant translational decision in the entire Pseudepigrapha project.

---

## 71:14 — 'born unto righteousness' — the nature of the Son of Man's birth

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "who-is-born-unto-righteousness" | Literal; Ge'ez za-wald la-sedeq |
| LOGOS | "who was born unto righteousness" | Past tense; the birth has already occurred |
| PNEUMA | "who was born to righteousness" | Slightly abbreviated; same meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Born unto righteousness' is the precise Ge'ez phrase. 'Unto' preserves the directional sense — born FOR righteousness, or born IN righteousness. The past tense ('was born') is correct.

**Two interpretive options exist:**
(a) Enoch's physical birth as a human being — who was then exalted. This makes the Son of Man a human being who was hidden in the heavenly realm.
(b) An eternal generation ('born' in the sense of Ps 2:7: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you'). This makes the Son of Man an eternally generated divine figure.

SOPHIA preserves the ambiguity by rendering the Ge'ez literally. Scholars divide between these options; the text is not definitive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Deliberate ambiguity preserved.

---

## 71:15 — 'world to come' — eschatological terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-name-of-the-world-to-come" | Literal; Ge'ez 'alam = world, age |
| LOGOS | "the name of the world to come" | Agrees; the coming age |
| PNEUMA | "the name of the age to come" | 'Age' for 'world' — both are valid for Ge'ez 'alam |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's 'world to come.' Both 'world' and 'age' are valid translations of 'alam (which covers both spatial and temporal meanings). 'World to come' (olam ha-ba) is the standard Second Temple eschatological formula and should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Technical eschatological term preserved.

---

## 71:5 — 'heaven of heavens' — the highest heaven

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-heaven-of-heavens" | Literal Ge'ez superlative construct |
| LOGOS | "the heaven of heavens" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "the heaven of heavens" | Agrees |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Full convergence. 'Heaven of heavens' is the Ge'ez superlative for the highest/innermost heaven — a construct also found in 1 Kgs 8:27 and Deut 10:14. All three translators preserve it.

**Status:** Full convergence.

---

## 71:7 — 'those who sleep not' — the unwearying guardians

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "these-are-they-who-sleep-not and-guard-the-throne" | Literal; unceasing vigilance |
| LOGOS | "these are they who sleep not and guard the throne of his glory" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "those who never sleep and who guard the throne of his glory" | 'Never sleep' for 'sleep not' — same meaning |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Who sleep not' is the traditional formula for the angelic guardians (cf. Isa 62:6). PNEUMA's 'never sleep' is equivalent but 'sleep not' preserves the archaic negation that suits the elevated register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
